Council

Members of the public are welcome to attend Council and Council Committee meetings. We encourage an interest in local issues and appreciate it when community members take the time to attend. All meeting details including times, dates, agendas and minutes are below.

Public attendance

  • These meetings are open to the public and you are welcome to attend.
  • The gallery capacity is 35 people. Once this limit is reached, access to the building will be closed to the public.
  • When you arrive, you will be asked to sign in. You will need to provide your name, phone number and have your photo taken.
  • Attendees in the gallery may be captured in the meeting recordings.

If you would like to attend the meeting, please register your interest below.

Registering helps us manage attendance numbers and ensure appropriate arrangement are in place, particularly for those wishing to observe a specific agenda item, such as a deputation or report.

Register your interest to attend

Council meeting livestream and recordings

All public Ordinary Council and Special Council meetings held in the Council Chamber at Ramsay Place, Noarlunga Centre will be livestreamed and recorded.

Members of the public are welcome to access the livestream to view the proceedings using the link below. 

While every effort will be made to ensure livestreaming is available, in the event that the livestream is disconnected, or technical issues arise, the meeting will continue uninterrupted.

Recordings will be made available to the public approximately 48 hours after the meeting.

Confidential items will not be livestreamed or recorded.

Watch on YouTube

Prior to the 20 June 2023, recorded meetings were only available for 24 months. Members of the public wishing to access a meeting recording no longer available will need to apply to council for access to the meeting recording. Please note that fees may apply.

Council Assessment Panel

The introduction of the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016 implemented changes that resulted in councils no longer being a relevant authority in their own right for planning or land division consents. Instead, councils must appoint an Assessment Manager and a Council Assessment Panel to perform the assessment functions on their behalf, and both are decision making authorities independent of council.

The City of Onkaparinga (the Council) resolved on 13 June 2017 to establish the City of Onkaparinga Council Assessment Panel (CAP) as a relevant authority under Sections 82 and 83 of the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016..  A Council Assessment Panel can only contain a maximum of one (1) Member of the Council (Elected Member), and one deputy Council Member, with the remaining being independent, accredited members, not being Members of the Council or State Parliament.

The CAP will undertake the assessment and determination of certain development applications, including those:

  • where representations from the public are to be heard
  • where the Minister has determined that the CAP is to be the relevant authority
  • any applications delegated from the Assessment Manager. 

The Council Assessment Panel consists of the following members:

  • Matt Atkinson (Chair)
  • Ross Bateup
  • Sarah Reachill 
  • Ben Schnell
  • John Byleveld (deputy independent member)
  • Cr Heidi Greaves
  • Cr Michael Fisher (deputy Council member)

Independent members of the CAP must be appropriately accredited and all members must abide by the state Assessment Panel Members Code of Conduct as found below.

Public attendance

  • These meetings are open to the public and you are welcome to attend.
  • The gallery capacity is 35 people. Once this limit is reached, access to the building will be closed to the public.
  • When you arrive, you will be asked to sign in. You will need to provide your name, phone number and have your photo taken.

Registering helps us manage attendance numbers.

Council

Members of the public are welcome to attend Council and Council Committee meetings. We encourage an interest in local issues and appreciate it when community members take the time to attend. All meeting details including times, dates, agendas and minutes are below.

Public attendance

  • These meetings are open to the public and you are welcome to attend.
  • The gallery capacity is 35 people. Once this limit is reached, access to the building will be closed to the public.
  • When you arrive, you will be asked to sign in. You will need to provide your name, phone number and have your photo taken.
  • Attendees in the gallery may be captured in the meeting recordings.

If you would like to attend the meeting, please register your interest below.

Registering helps us manage attendance numbers and ensure appropriate arrangement are in place, particularly for those wishing to observe a specific agenda item, such as a deputation or report.

Register your interest to attend

Council meeting livestream and recordings

All public Ordinary Council and Special Council meetings held in the Council Chamber at Ramsay Place, Noarlunga Centre will be livestreamed and recorded.

Members of the public are welcome to access the livestream to view the proceedings using the link below. 

While every effort will be made to ensure livestreaming is available, in the event that the livestream is disconnected, or technical issues arise, the meeting will continue uninterrupted.

Recordings will be made available to the public approximately 48 hours after the meeting.

Confidential items will not be livestreamed or recorded.

Watch on YouTube

Prior to the 20 June 2023, recorded meetings were only available for 24 months. Members of the public wishing to access a meeting recording no longer available will need to apply to council for access to the meeting recording. Please note that fees may apply.

Council

Members of the public are welcome to attend Council and Council Committee meetings. We encourage an interest in local issues and appreciate it when community members take the time to attend. All meeting details including times, dates, agendas and minutes are below.

Public attendance

  • These meetings are open to the public and you are welcome to attend.
  • The gallery capacity is 35 people. Once this limit is reached, access to the building will be closed to the public.
  • When you arrive, you will be asked to sign in. You will need to provide your name, phone number and have your photo taken.
  • Attendees in the gallery may be captured in the meeting recordings.

If you would like to attend the meeting, please register your interest below.

Registering helps us manage attendance numbers and ensure appropriate arrangement are in place, particularly for those wishing to observe a specific agenda item, such as a deputation or report.

Register your interest to attend

Council meeting livestream and recordings

All public Ordinary Council and Special Council meetings held in the Council Chamber at Ramsay Place, Noarlunga Centre will be livestreamed and recorded.

Members of the public are welcome to access the livestream to view the proceedings using the link below. 

While every effort will be made to ensure livestreaming is available, in the event that the livestream is disconnected, or technical issues arise, the meeting will continue uninterrupted.

Recordings will be made available to the public approximately 48 hours after the meeting.

Confidential items will not be livestreamed or recorded.

Watch on YouTube

Prior to the 20 June 2023, recorded meetings were only available for 24 months. Members of the public wishing to access a meeting recording no longer available will need to apply to council for access to the meeting recording. Please note that fees may apply.

Council

Members of the public are welcome to attend Council and Council Committee meetings. We encourage an interest in local issues and appreciate it when community members take the time to attend. All meeting details including times, dates, agendas and minutes are below.

Public attendance

  • These meetings are open to the public and you are welcome to attend.
  • The gallery capacity is 35 people. Once this limit is reached, access to the building will be closed to the public.
  • When you arrive, you will be asked to sign in. You will need to provide your name, phone number and have your photo taken.
  • Attendees in the gallery may be captured in the meeting recordings.

If you would like to attend the meeting, please register your interest below.

Registering helps us manage attendance numbers and ensure appropriate arrangement are in place, particularly for those wishing to observe a specific agenda item, such as a deputation or report.

Register your interest to attend

Council meeting livestream and recordings

All public Ordinary Council and Special Council meetings held in the Council Chamber at Ramsay Place, Noarlunga Centre will be livestreamed and recorded.

Members of the public are welcome to access the livestream to view the proceedings using the link below. 

While every effort will be made to ensure livestreaming is available, in the event that the livestream is disconnected, or technical issues arise, the meeting will continue uninterrupted.

Recordings will be made available to the public approximately 48 hours after the meeting.

Confidential items will not be livestreamed or recorded.

Watch on YouTube

Prior to the 20 June 2023, recorded meetings were only available for 24 months. Members of the public wishing to access a meeting recording no longer available will need to apply to council for access to the meeting recording. Please note that fees may apply.

Council

Members of the public are welcome to attend Council and Council Committee meetings. We encourage an interest in local issues and appreciate it when community members take the time to attend. All meeting details including times, dates, agendas and minutes are below.

Public attendance

  • These meetings are open to the public and you are welcome to attend.
  • The gallery capacity is 35 people. Once this limit is reached, access to the building will be closed to the public.
  • When you arrive, you will be asked to sign in. You will need to provide your name, phone number and have your photo taken.
  • Attendees in the gallery may be captured in the meeting recordings.

If you would like to attend the meeting, please register your interest below.

Registering helps us manage attendance numbers and ensure appropriate arrangement are in place, particularly for those wishing to observe a specific agenda item, such as a deputation or report.

Register your interest to attend

Council meeting livestream and recordings

All public Ordinary Council and Special Council meetings held in the Council Chamber at Ramsay Place, Noarlunga Centre will be livestreamed and recorded.

Members of the public are welcome to access the livestream to view the proceedings using the link below. 

While every effort will be made to ensure livestreaming is available, in the event that the livestream is disconnected, or technical issues arise, the meeting will continue uninterrupted.

Recordings will be made available to the public approximately 48 hours after the meeting.

Confidential items will not be livestreamed or recorded.

Watch on YouTube

Prior to the 20 June 2023, recorded meetings were only available for 24 months. Members of the public wishing to access a meeting recording no longer available will need to apply to council for access to the meeting recording. Please note that fees may apply.

Council Assessment Panel

The introduction of the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016 implemented changes that resulted in councils no longer being a relevant authority in their own right for planning or land division consents. Instead, councils must appoint an Assessment Manager and a Council Assessment Panel to perform the assessment functions on their behalf, and both are decision making authorities independent of council.

The City of Onkaparinga (the Council) resolved on 13 June 2017 to establish the City of Onkaparinga Council Assessment Panel (CAP) as a relevant authority under Sections 82 and 83 of the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016..  A Council Assessment Panel can only contain a maximum of one (1) Member of the Council (Elected Member), and one deputy Council Member, with the remaining being independent, accredited members, not being Members of the Council or State Parliament.

The CAP will undertake the assessment and determination of certain development applications, including those:

  • where representations from the public are to be heard
  • where the Minister has determined that the CAP is to be the relevant authority
  • any applications delegated from the Assessment Manager. 

The Council Assessment Panel consists of the following members:

  • Matt Atkinson (Chair)
  • Ross Bateup
  • Sarah Reachill 
  • Ben Schnell
  • John Byleveld (deputy independent member)
  • Cr Heidi Greaves
  • Cr Michael Fisher (deputy Council member)

Independent members of the CAP must be appropriately accredited and all members must abide by the state Assessment Panel Members Code of Conduct as found below.

  • The gallery capacity is 35 people. Once this limit is reached, access to the building will be closed to the public.

Council Assessment Panel

The introduction of the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016 implemented changes that resulted in councils no longer being a relevant authority in their own right for planning or land division consents. Instead, councils must appoint an Assessment Manager and a Council Assessment Panel to perform the assessment functions on their behalf, and both are decision making authorities independent of council.

The City of Onkaparinga (the Council) resolved on 13 June 2017 to establish the City of Onkaparinga Council Assessment Panel (CAP) as a relevant authority under Sections 82 and 83 of the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016..  A Council Assessment Panel can only contain a maximum of one (1) Member of the Council (Elected Member), and one deputy Council Member, with the remaining being independent, accredited members, not being Members of the Council or State Parliament.

The CAP will undertake the assessment and determination of certain development applications, including those:

  • where representations from the public are to be heard
  • where the Minister has determined that the CAP is to be the relevant authority
  • any applications delegated from the Assessment Manager. 

The Council Assessment Panel consists of the following members:

  • Matt Atkinson (Chair)
  • Ross Bateup
  • Sarah Reachill 
  • Ben Schnell
  • John Byleveld (deputy independent member)
  • Cr Heidi Greaves
  • Cr Michael Fisher (deputy Council member)

Independent members of the CAP must be appropriately accredited and all members must abide by the state Assessment Panel Members Code of Conduct as found below.

Public attendance

  • These meetings are open to the public and you are welcome to attend.
  • The gallery capacity is 35 people. Once this limit is reached, access to the building will be closed to the public.
  • When you arrive, you will be asked to sign in. You will need to provide your name, phone number and have your photo taken.

Registering helps us manage attendance numbers.

Council Assessment Panel

The introduction of the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016 implemented changes that resulted in councils no longer being a relevant authority in their own right for planning or land division consents. Instead, councils must appoint an Assessment Manager and a Council Assessment Panel to perform the assessment functions on their behalf, and both are decision making authorities independent of council.

The City of Onkaparinga (the Council) resolved on 13 June 2017 to establish the City of Onkaparinga Council Assessment Panel (CAP) as a relevant authority under Sections 82 and 83 of the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016..  A Council Assessment Panel can only contain a maximum of one (1) Member of the Council (Elected Member), and one deputy Council Member, with the remaining being independent, accredited members, not being Members of the Council or State Parliament.

The CAP will undertake the assessment and determination of certain development applications, including those:

  • where representations from the public are to be heard
  • where the Minister has determined that the CAP is to be the relevant authority
  • any applications delegated from the Assessment Manager. 

The Council Assessment Panel consists of the following members:

  • Matt Atkinson (Chair)
  • Ross Bateup
  • Sarah Reachill 
  • Ben Schnell
  • John Byleveld (deputy independent member)
  • Cr Heidi Greaves
  • Cr Michael Fisher (deputy Council member)

Independent members of the CAP must be appropriately accredited and all members must abide by the state Assessment Panel Members Code of Conduct as found below.

Public attendance

  • These meetings are open to the public and you are welcome to attend.
  • The gallery capacity is 35 people. Once this limit is reached, access to the building will be closed to the public.
  • When you arrive, you will be asked to sign in. You will need to provide your name, phone number and have your photo taken.

Registering helps us manage attendance numbers.

Council Assessment Panel

The introduction of the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016 implemented changes that resulted in councils no longer being a relevant authority in their own right for planning or land division consents. Instead, councils must appoint an Assessment Manager and a Council Assessment Panel to perform the assessment functions on their behalf, and both are decision making authorities independent of council.

The City of Onkaparinga (the Council) resolved on 13 June 2017 to establish the City of Onkaparinga Council Assessment Panel (CAP) as a relevant authority under Sections 82 and 83 of the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016..  A Council Assessment Panel can only contain a maximum of one (1) Member of the Council (Elected Member), and one deputy Council Member, with the remaining being independent, accredited members, not being Members of the Council or State Parliament.

The CAP will undertake the assessment and determination of certain development applications, including those:

  • where representations from the public are to be heard
  • where the Minister has determined that the CAP is to be the relevant authority
  • any applications delegated from the Assessment Manager. 

The Council Assessment Panel consists of the following members:

  • Matt Atkinson (Chair)
  • Ross Bateup
  • Sarah Reachill 
  • Ben Schnell
  • John Byleveld (deputy independent member)
  • Cr Heidi Greaves
  • Cr Michael Fisher (deputy Council member)

Independent members of the CAP must be appropriately accredited and all members must abide by the state Assessment Panel Members Code of Conduct as found below.

Public attendance

  • These meetings are open to the public and you are welcome to attend.
  • The gallery capacity is 35 people. Once this limit is reached, access to the building will be closed to the public.
  • When you arrive, you will be asked to sign in. You will need to provide your name, phone number and have your photo taken.

Registering helps us manage attendance numbers.

Council Assessment Panel

The introduction of the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016 implemented changes that resulted in councils no longer being a relevant authority in their own right for planning or land division consents. Instead, councils must appoint an Assessment Manager and a Council Assessment Panel to perform the assessment functions on their behalf, and both are decision making authorities independent of council.

The City of Onkaparinga (the Council) resolved on 13 June 2017 to establish the City of Onkaparinga Council Assessment Panel (CAP) as a relevant authority under Sections 82 and 83 of the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016..  A Council Assessment Panel can only contain a maximum of one (1) Member of the Council (Elected Member), and one deputy Council Member, with the remaining being independent, accredited members, not being Members of the Council or State Parliament.

The CAP will undertake the assessment and determination of certain development applications, including those:

  • where representations from the public are to be heard
  • where the Minister has determined that the CAP is to be the relevant authority
  • any applications delegated from the Assessment Manager. 

The Council Assessment Panel consists of the following members:

  • Matt Atkinson (Chair)
  • Ross Bateup
  • Sarah Reachill 
  • Ben Schnell
  • John Byleveld (deputy independent member)
  • Cr Heidi Greaves
  • Cr Michael Fisher (deputy Council member)

Independent members of the CAP must be appropriately accredited and all members must abide by the state Assessment Panel Members Code of Conduct as found below.

Public attendance

  • These meetings are open to the public and you are welcome to attend.
  • The gallery capacity is 35 people. Once this limit is reached, access to the building will be closed to the public.
  • When you arrive, you will be asked to sign in. You will need to provide your name, phone number and have your photo taken.

Registering helps us manage attendance numbers.

Council Assessment Panel

The introduction of the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016 implemented changes that resulted in councils no longer being a relevant authority in their own right for planning or land division consents. Instead, councils must appoint an Assessment Manager and a Council Assessment Panel to perform the assessment functions on their behalf, and both are decision making authorities independent of council.

The City of Onkaparinga (the Council) resolved on 13 June 2017 to establish the City of Onkaparinga Council Assessment Panel (CAP) as a relevant authority under Sections 82 and 83 of the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016..  A Council Assessment Panel can only contain a maximum of one (1) Member of the Council (Elected Member), and one deputy Council Member, with the remaining being independent, accredited members, not being Members of the Council or State Parliament.

The CAP will undertake the assessment and determination of certain development applications, including those:

  • where representations from the public are to be heard
  • where the Minister has determined that the CAP is to be the relevant authority
  • any applications delegated from the Assessment Manager. 

The Council Assessment Panel consists of the following members:

  • Matt Atkinson (Chair)
  • Ross Bateup
  • Sarah Reachill 
  • Ben Schnell
  • John Byleveld (deputy independent member)
  • Cr Heidi Greaves
  • Cr Michael Fisher (deputy Council member)

Independent members of the CAP must be appropriately accredited and all members must abide by the state Assessment Panel Members Code of Conduct as found below.

Public attendance

  • These meetings are open to the public and you are welcome to attend.
  • The gallery capacity is 35 people. Once this limit is reached, access to the building will be closed to the public.
  • When you arrive, you will be asked to sign in. You will need to provide your name, phone number and have your photo taken.

Registering helps us manage attendance numbers.

Council Assessment Panel

The introduction of the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016 implemented changes that resulted in councils no longer being a relevant authority in their own right for planning or land division consents. Instead, councils must appoint an Assessment Manager and a Council Assessment Panel to perform the assessment functions on their behalf, and both are decision making authorities independent of council.

The City of Onkaparinga (the Council) resolved on 13 June 2017 to establish the City of Onkaparinga Council Assessment Panel (CAP) as a relevant authority under Sections 82 and 83 of the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016..  A Council Assessment Panel can only contain a maximum of one (1) Member of the Council (Elected Member), and one deputy Council Member, with the remaining being independent, accredited members, not being Members of the Council or State Parliament.

The CAP will undertake the assessment and determination of certain development applications, including those:

  • where representations from the public are to be heard
  • where the Minister has determined that the CAP is to be the relevant authority
  • any applications delegated from the Assessment Manager. 

The Council Assessment Panel consists of the following members:

  • Matt Atkinson (Chair)
  • Ross Bateup
  • Sarah Reachill 
  • Ben Schnell
  • John Byleveld (deputy independent member)
  • Cr Heidi Greaves
  • Cr Michael Fisher (deputy Council member)

Independent members of the CAP must be appropriately accredited and all members must abide by the state Assessment Panel Members Code of Conduct as found below.

Public attendance

  • These meetings are open to the public and you are welcome to attend.
  • The gallery capacity is 35 people. Once this limit is reached, access to the building will be closed to the public.
  • When you arrive, you will be asked to sign in. You will need to provide your name, phone number and have your photo taken.
